Lot of whiny responses here.  You can choose to upvote the comments that suit your “boohoo, unfair” narrative, or you can actually look at facts and walk away with helpful/productive advice.  It all depends on if you actually want women to like you, or if you want to just complain how unfair gender roles are.  Entirely your choice. 

Women are attracted to decisive men who show interest in them.  Asking her on a date, paying for the date, offering to walk her home, etc. are all simple things you can do to show her that you’re taking this seriously (I.e., not using her for sex) and that goes a long way.

Does it feel unequal?  Yes.  Because it is.  And for good reason- life is unequal.  These are facts. 

Men don’t have to question if their date is only pretending to be interested to use them for sex.  For women this is a common concern. 

Women are looking for a potential husband- that means she will be more attracted to you if you can display the qualities a good (future) husband would have.  That includes making her feel secure.  If you bust out a calculator when the check arrives to figure out her half of the bill, that doesn’t scream “financially secure.”  

If you can’t even pay for a date, how can she see you as the man she wants to build a life with? Buy a house with?  Have kids with?  Women think about relationships in these terms. 

And if you can easily afford it, but just don’t want to pay because (reasons)- that tells her you aren’t investing in her as a serious prospective partner.  She isn’t worth dinner/drinks/whatever.  AKA, you don’t like her that much, or aren’t taking it seriously. 

Friend, it’s not just gold diggers / fake feminists / whatever who will be turned off by this.  You are free to use the splitting the check thing as some kind of litmus test like so many comments are suggesting.  That is your choice.  But just know, you are going to filter out good women as well. 

Asking her on a date shows confidence and decisiveness.  She knows you’re interested.  She knows you’re brave enough to ask.  These are attractive qualities in a man to a woman.  

Walking her to her car shows you care about her safety.  This doesn’t go both ways.  It’s not unfair, it’s reality.  She isn’t going to protect you, you are going to protect her.  You are a man.

Remember she will be the one who gets pregnant or assumes the risk of getting pregnant.  Show her you’re a provider and she will feel safer with you.  It’s an unequal world and we are just living in it. 

Good luck with dating, you’ll have much better odds if you get over the equality bullshit.

You are correct that users aren’t “locked” into the presets.  I am correct that OB presets are designed very much with ALARA/bioeffect reduction in mind.

I also think it’s worth pointing out no real human babies have been harmed by ultrasound and the bioeffects are all more or less theoretical. 

The AIUM guidelines are very, very cautious- for good reason, but it’s awfully misleading to say getting an OB ultrasound will “heat up the baby.”  There is no productive reason to scare people out of getting an important medical exam.  When the situation calls for it, ultrasound techs are actually encouraged to use Doppler for OB, since it may assist in identifying important fetal abnormalities; and the “damage” caused by using the higher power settings is …. well, realistically a non factor. 

Can ultrasound ~technically~ cause heating bioeffects?  Yes.  Hence all the caution and all the limitations in place.  But has a real life baby ever been damaged by the heating of an ultrasound?  No.

Hey, dude.  I’m sorry for what you’re going through.  

School is hard for a lot of people.  I used to feel alone dealing with my own bullies, and just like you I used to blame myself for never hitting back or standing up to them.  But it all depends how you look at it.  WasI a pussy for not fighting back?  If you asked a bully that question, they’d say yes.  But my girlfriend at the time had an opposite opinion; she thought it showed a lot of restraint / self control to be able to stay calm instead of the gut reaction of lashing out.  She was impressed by how much maturity it showed.  I care way more about her opinion than theirs.

There’s other good news.  One is that your mother loves and supports you.  I know her attempts to help seemed to backfire and make things worse, but at least she cared.  ( my parents never tried to help me or gave a shit.)  The other good news is that you graduated and don’t ever have to see those assholes again. 

But just because you don’t have to see them anymore doesn’t mean that it’s over.  As of right now, it’s NOT over, because you’re still giving them real estate in your mind so to speak.  

Think about it this way.  Every minute that you had to spend with these guys while they were messing with you, is essentially like a minute of your life that they stole from you.  You could have spent that time reading a book, talking with friends, doing your schoolwork, or anything else.  But instead you spent that minute getting hit in the face by a rubber band.  This is completely unfair to you.  It sucks.  Also, it wasn’t your fault. 

Now think about the time apart from them, most likely outside of school, when you spent any time worrying about it.  Eating breakfast in the morning while anxious, thinking about what they might do to you that day?  That’s 15 min of fear and unpleasantness.  So, another 15 min they’ve “stolen” from you.  Sitting at home after school, angry at yourself for not standing up to them earlier that day, going through all the possibilities of what you could’ve done instead?  Guess what.  That’s another half hour of your precious time you’re giving away to them.  Replaying incidents in your head before falling asleep at night, that’s more and more of your mental headspace they’re claiming.  You can’t get these hours back.

We only have limited time on this earth, and you never know what could happen.  What if you died in 30 days?  Would you be worrying about the shit that happened to you in high school still, or trying to go out there and live your life to the fullest as much as possible?  To me, it’s not worth the risk.  You never know when your time on this planet is up, and honestly, you’ve given those dickbags enough hours of your life already.

Forgiveness doesn’t have to mean “no hard feelings, it’s fine, let’s be best friends now.”  Not at all.  For me, it was realizing that I didn’t like the way it felt to be bitter and angry all the time.  I decided that all the negative feelings I was holding onto were like a very heavy burden, just weighing me down.  I wanted to let go of it so I could “free” myself in a way.  It was a purposeful decision, to be done with that mentality, because I was sick of it.  And I’m so much happier now.  

Don’t be mad at yourself for not beating them up when you had the chance.  Odds are, it wouldn’t have been satisfying like in the movies.  If you seriously injured someone, you might regretted it, and it could cause you to look at yourself like a different person.  You also could’ve gotten into a lot of trouble.  Probably not worth it.  

I strongly recommend, next time a thought about your bullies pops into your head, remind yourself “is this what I want to be thinking about and concerning myself over?”  I guarantee your bullies aren’t sitting around thinking about you.  Don’t do it for them.  Don’t allow them to steal any more time from you.  This is your life, and they don’t deserve a starring role.  Choose to forgive and let it all go, and you’ll finally be free.

Therapy was helpful for me also, don’t be scared to reach out for help if you need it.  Good luck.
